Welcome to Stelling Minnis CE Primary School
A warm welcome to Stelling Minnis Church of England Primary School, nestled between the beautiful villages of Bossingham and Stelling Minnis, we are conveniently close to Canterbury, Ashford and Folkestone.
Our school is a beacon of light. A place where every child and adult is encouraged to shine brightly and reach their full potential. Through curiosity, courage, and compassion, we shine like a lamp in our classrooms, like a village on a hill in our community, and like shining stars across the wider world.
Many people choose our school due to its family feel and values as well as our unique offer of academic excellence with a substantive nurturing offer of farm school and outdoor learning. We do encourage you to come and see our wonderful school, marvellous environment and our incredible children for yourselves. Please get in touch to arrange a tour.

Religious Education Curriculum
Religious Education Shines Brightly at Stelling Minnis...
At Stelling Minnis Church of England Primary School, Religious Education (RE) is taught through regular lessons in every class. Our RE curriculum enables pupils to explore Christianity and other major world faiths and beliefs, helping them to understand the world around them and reflect on their own ideas and values.
We use the Understanding Christianity resource to support our teaching of Christianity. This resource is designed to help pupils develop their own thinking while gaining a deep and meaningful understanding of Christian belief and practice as well as other world faiths such as Judaism, Islam, Sikhism and Hinduism.
Understanding Christianity provides a coherent and progressive approach to teaching Christianity across the school. It focuses on eight core Christian concepts that sit at the heart of mainstream Christian belief, such as Creation, Incarnation, Salvation and Kingdom of God.
The resource supports learning through three key elements:
Each unit focuses on a core concept and is taught through key questions, carefully chosen Bible passages, and discussion about how belief influences action. Over time, pupils build secure knowledge and understanding, supported by clear progression and age-appropriate expectations.
When studying other faiths and beliefs, our teaching also follows two important strands:
Pupils’ learning is assessed against clear knowledge “building blocks” and end-of-phase outcomes. This ensures progression in knowledge, understanding and skills, and supports children in becoming confident, reflective learners who can engage thoughtfully with religious ideas and texts.
Through our RE curriculum, we aim to nurture curiosity, respect and understanding, while supporting pupils in exploring faith, belief and meaning in a diverse and changing world.
Parents may remove their child from any/ all RE lessons.

Speaking & Listening
At Stelling Minnis Primary School, we believe that every child deserves to be heard. Oracy—speaking and listening effectively—is central to our curriculum and underpins all learning.
From EYFS, children are immersed in a language-rich environment where they learn to express ideas, listen carefully and take turns through play, storytelling and discussion. As they move through the school, these skills are developed through structured opportunities to talk, collaborate, debate and present across all subjects.
Key strands running through EYFS–Year 6
Listening and attention – from sustained attention and following instructions to critical listening and evaluating viewpoints.
Vocabulary and language – from developing vocabulary to selecting precise language for audience and purpose.
Discussion and interaction – from turn-taking to leading, challenging and negotiating within discussions.
Questioning – from asking and answering simple questions to asking insightful questions that deepen understanding.
Reasoning and justification – from explaining preferences to constructing reasoned arguments supported by evidence.
Presentation – from speaking to a small group to delivering confident presentations to a range of audiences.
Performance – from rhymes, songs and role play to expressive performance and formal speaking.
Audience and purpose – from familiar contexts to deliberately adapting register, vocabulary, tone and delivery.
Confidence and fluency – developing the ability to speak clearly, confidently and spontaneously.
Reflection – increasingly evaluating the effectiveness of their own and others’ spoken communication.

Mathematics Curriculum
At Stelling Minnis, our mathematics curriculum is built on the principles and structure of White Rose Maths, ensuring every child develops deep, secure and adaptable understanding. Teaching is rooted in the mastery approach, where learning progresses in carefully planned small steps so that pupils build knowledge cumulatively and confidently.
We develop pupils’ mathematical fluency, reasoning and problem‑solving through rich, coherent sequences of learning. These sequences are underpinned by the key curriculum threads of number, geometry, measurement, statistics and algebra, which spiral progressively through the school to strengthen long‑term understanding.
Our curriculum deliberately promotes a balance of declarative knowledge (facts and concepts pupils need to know), procedural knowledge (methods and steps they need to apply) and conditional knowledge (knowing when and why to use a particular strategy). This supports children in becoming flexible, independent mathematicians able to apply their learning in a range of contexts.
To ensure clarity and precision in mathematical communication, each unit includes carefully mapped vocabulary, introduced and revisited systematically to help pupils articulate their thinking and develop confident reasoning skills.
Through this structured, inclusive and ambitious approach, Stelling Minnis aims to empower every learner to enjoy maths, understand it deeply and use it purposefully.
Guides for parents
White Rose Maths have teamed up with TV presenter, teacher and parent Michael Underwood to bring you a mini-series called Maths with Michael. These mini videos will help explain how maths is taught in school and how you may support your child. We have also added some resources to explain each unit that is taught in school during your child's time with us.
Maths with Michael | Michael Underwood | White Rose Maths (whiteroseeducation.com)
Stelling Minnis CE Primary School weaves LEAF Education principles into its maths curriculum in a practical, engaging, and sustainability‑focused way. Through our work with LEAF, pupils explore real farming contexts that bring mathematical concepts to life, helping them understand how numbers shape the world around them—particularly in food production and environmental stewardship.
Where possible,, children use real‑world farm data to practise skills such as measurement, estimation, multiplication, and financial calculations. Sustainability sits at the heart of this approach: pupils learn how farmers balance productivity with caring for the land, and teachers use these themes to frame maths tasks that highlight responsible resource use, seasonal cycles, and the long‑term impact of farming decisions.
Some of our pupils were keen to work out how many weeks of pocket money it would take to buy their own combine harvester!

Our Curriculum Vision
At Stelling Minnis CE Primary School, our vision is to be a beacon of light—a place where every child and adult is encouraged to shine brightly, guided by our Christian values of curiosity, courage and compassion. We celebrate our rich rural landscape whilst ensuring that our children are inspired, supported, and equipped for life beyond the village. We aim to broaden horizons and nurture global citizens who can shine confidently “like a lamp in our classrooms, like a village on a hill in our community, and like shining stars across the wider world.”
We bring our vision to life through high-quality teaching, carefully sequenced learning and rich, purposeful experiences. Our bespoke curriculum combines the explicit teaching of knowledge and skills with opportunities for exploration, enquiry and application through our Core Concepts, Farm School, Forest School and Opportunities to Shine. Through modelling, retrieval practice, rich vocabulary and meaningful real-life contexts, children develop secure understanding over time. Starting with strong foundations in EYFS, learning builds progressively, enabling all pupils to deepen knowledge, master key skills and connect learning across the curriculum.
Our pupils leave Stelling Minnis as curious, courageous and compassionate young people who are ready to shine even more brightly. They have strong academic foundations, a deep sense of belonging to their community, and the confidence to embrace new challenges. They can think critically, make meaningful connections in their learning and understand their role in the wider world. Equipped with the knowledge, skills and character to thrive, they are well prepared for the next stage of their education and beyond.
If you require more information about our curriculum and subjects, please navigate the curriculum area of the website to find more detailed information about each subject. Alternatively, you may contact the school office who will be able to direct you.
Our Curriculum runs on a two Year cycle which is common in small schools.
2025, 2027 and 2029 will follow Cycle A. 2026, 2028 and 2030 will follow Cycle B.

Pupil & Sports Premium
Barriers to learning:
These are some of the barriers to learning that affect some of the pupils to varying extents. No single eligible pupil has all these barriers to learning.
1. Increasing Staff Confidence, Knowledge and Skills
Specialist sports coaches have worked alongside staff to deliver high-quality PE lessons, model effective practice and improve teacher confidence. Staff subject knowledge has increased so that they may in turn start to provide additional sessions for the children through clubs or opportunities such as the Minnis Mile and external marathon events.
2. Increasing Engagement in Regular Physical Activity
Forest School sessions have provided regular opportunities for all pupils to take part in active outdoor learning. Pupils have developed physical skills, teamwork, resilience and confidence while increasing overall activity levels. Farm School offers physical therapeutic experiences.
3. Raising the Profile of PE and Sport
Physical activity remains a significant part of school life through PE lessons, Forest School, sporting events and celebration of achievements. This has promoted positive attitudes towards healthy lifestyles and wellbeing.
4. Broadening Sporting Experiences
Funding for clubs, equipment and enrichment opportunities has enabled pupils to experience a wider range of activities and increased participation amongst different pupil groups. Forest school club has proven to be as popular as our formal sports club
5. Participation in Competitive Sport
District sports competitions and educational visits such as Hindleap Warren have enabled pupils to represent the school, develop sportsmanship, teamwork and resilience, and participate in competitive activities.

· Engage a new sport coaching provider
· Maintain Forest School provision as a key aspect of outdoor learning and physical development.

Reading
At Stelling Minnis CE Primary School we value reading as the basis of our whole curriculum! From the moment a child is born they begin to acquire the skills for reading through language and vocabulary and we continue that learning journey from day one at our school. We have built a high quality reading curriculum to guide our young people to be life-long readers with both skill and passion.
The tools we use to support our reading curriculum are:
At the core of each unit of study, high quality texts such as Power of Reading books, as recommended by the CLPE (Centre for Literacy in Primary Education), are carefully selected based on their theme and content. These books are shared as whole class core texts to ensure that all children at Stelling Minnis are exposed to quality literature; broadening and deepening their knowledge and comprehension with regular opportunities to discuss, reflect and respond.
This approach resonates through every other reading experience children encounter, such as whole class reading, group reading sessions, peer reading and in selecting the books which we provide for children to read independently, and the contexts we provide for sharing and enjoying these books. Pupils read at frequent intervals during the school week; to staff, at home, to parent-helpers, during quiet reading times, as well as for research in other subjects.
Daily reading comprehension takes place, taught through the unit of study texts, as well as weekly discrete reading skills lessons.

Science
At Stelling Minnis, we nurture confident, curious learners who think, question, and explore like scientists. We provide a rich and engaging science curriculum built on the Kent Primary Science Scheme of Work, ensuring clear progression in both knowledge and skills.
Science is taught through hands-on, practical experiences, enabling pupils to explore, investigate and develop a deep understanding of the world around them. Through carefully planned lessons, children are encouraged to be curious, ask questions and learn through discovery.
A strong emphasis is placed on developing science enquiry skills (working scientifically). Pupils learn to ask questions, make predictions, carry out investigations, observe and measure, record results and draw conclusions as well as learning about the work of real life scientists.
